subject: gk
question:
Find the odd one out.

Vacuoles, Nucleus, Ribosomes, Lysosomes
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ribosomes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ribosomes** are the odd one out because they are not membrane-bound organelles, unlike the other options.
 
• Ribosomes are involved in **protein synthesis** and are found either floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the endoplasmic reticulum.
 
• They are composed of **ribosomal RNA (rRNA)** and proteins.
 
• The primary function of ribosomes is to translate messenger RNA (mRNA) into proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nucleus**__

 __
 
• The **nucleus** is a membrane-bound organelle that contains the cell's genetic material (DNA).
 
• It controls cellular activities by regulating gene expression.
 
• The nucleus is surrounded by the **nuclear envelope**, which has pores to allow the exchange of materials.
 
 
 
• **Vacuoles**__
 __
 
• **Vacuoles** are membrane-bound organelles found in plant and fungal cells, and some protist, animal, and bacterial cells.
 
• They are responsible for the storage of nutrients, waste products, and maintaining turgor pressure in plant cells.
 
• In animal cells, vacuoles are generally smaller and more numerous.
 
 
 
• **Lysosomes**__
 
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound organelles containing digestive enzymes.
 
• They break down excess or worn-out cell parts, and can be involved in destroying invading viruses and bacteria.
 
• Lysosomes are often called the "stomach" of the cell due to their role in digestion.
